correctness.rationale: The explicit graph definition yields 17 vertices, 68 edges, 68 triangles and no K4. The chosen 16-edge tree gives exactly 52 generators and 68 triangle relators. Every one of 52 legally applicable unique-occurrence Tietze eliminations is recomputed in the attached standalone Python verifier, ending with all generators removed and 16 empty relators, so pi1 is trivial; Euler/Hurewicz/Whitehead then imply the 16-sphere wedge and free integral H2. The exact action on oriented simplices was checked for all 136 affine group elements; Hopf trace plus rational character theory proves the module identification. Exhaustive diameter-two verification gives the Rips barcode. Computations apply to this finite complex only.

evidence: Cioabă–Guo–Ji–Mim, arxiv:2508.05871 PDF page 31, following Theorem 5.21, includes Paley(17) in a verified list with H^1(Cl(Paley17);R)=0. It does not report pi1 or the affine H2 action.

Cioabă–Mim, arxiv:2606.27328 introductory classification isolates possible nonvanishing H1 cases and gives broader first-homology criteria, not a fundamental-group or homotopy classification of Paley17.
Gallo–Videla, arxiv:2303.04312, Sections 3–4 concern clique counts for generalized Paley graphs, not π1 or equivariant homology.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Known vanishing H1 (even over all fields) does not imply simple connectivity; a perfect nontrivial group could survive abelianization. Similarly ordinary Betti ranks, even exact, do not determine a group character. The new Tietze certificate supplies genuinely additional nonabelian information.

originality.rationale: The closest 2025 primary paper explicitly verifies vanishing first real cohomology for the same Paley-17 clique complex (Section 5, p31 PDF); together with f-vector this covers Betti ranks. However, its linear first-cohomology computation does not determine the nonabelian fundamental group, so it cannot imply the claimed wedge homotopy type. Its results also do not give the full 136-element affine homology character. The 2023 Paley clique-count work provides counting formulas rather than attaching-map or module information. Semantic search of published related records using exact graph, conference-graph aliases, complement/independence duality, and symmetry terms returned related but different complex/graph results; absence in search is not a uniqueness certificate. Finite rational-character calculation is proved independently from signed chain actions.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named computation could already state the exact Paley17 wedge type or affine module.
Published 2025 first-cohomology vanishing together with classical f-vector data covers ordinary rational Betti ranks; those ranks are not novel.
The rational character is not a statement about integral group-module extensions or equivariant homotopy equivalence.

value.rationale: The seventeen-vertex Paley graph is a canonical strongly regular, extremal Ramsey and self-complementary graph. Its actual homotopy type and affine symmetry action are natural exact invariants extending published purely homological and face-count information. The nonabelian pi1 certificate rules out a perfect-group obstruction undetectable by H1 and gives a concrete integral wedge classification; the 136-element character distinguishes the representation from Betti-number-only results. The finite complete classification is valuable on its own, without a general result for all Paley orders.
